pr.title: Rebrand the product as ArzoieMail
pr.body:
## Summary

Gives the fork its own identity. Everything users see now says **ArzoieMail**, and fresh installations go to their own folders. The names that existing installations, scripts and WebAdmin depend on stay as they are.

| | Now ArzoieMail | Still hMailServer (on purpose) |
|---|---|---|
| Installer | Title, setup file `ArzoieMail-<ver>-B<n>-x64-Setup.exe`, Programs and Features entry, Start menu, messages | `AppId`, so it upgrades an hMailServer install in place |
| Folders (new installs) | `C:\Program Files\ArzoieMail`, `C:\ProgramData\ArzoieMail` | Upgraded installs keep their `hMailServer` folders |
| Windows service | Display name in Services | Service name, `NT SERVICE\hMailServer`, `net start hMailServer` |
| Programs | Version info, window titles, dialogs, About box | `hMailServer.exe`, `hMailAdmin.exe`, `hMailServer.ini` |
| Administrator text | English text and all 38 translations | `X-hMailServer-*` header names, the old version names DBUpdater lists |
| API / data | — | `hMailServer.Application` COM API, registry keys, `hm_` tables |
| CI | Artifact, release and tag names | — |

## How upgrades keep working

- The server, installer and tests look for `hMailServer.ini` in `ProgramData\ArzoieMail` first, then in `ProgramData\hMailServer`.
- The installer keeps `AppId=hMailServer`. Without that, Inno Setup would derive the ID from the new name, and an existing installation would no longer be recognised as one to upgrade.
- The service's display name is also updated when an existing service is reconfigured during an upgrade.
- The installer's "close this program first" check recognises both the old and new tool window titles.

## Also fixed

- The installer's "this program requires…" message said Windows Vista SP2. It now says Windows 10 / Server 2016, which the previous PR made the minimum.

## Tests

- New `Infrastructure\ProductIdentity` regression tests check:
  - the service name is unchanged,
  - the service display name is ArzoieMail,
  - `hMailServer.exe` reports ArzoieMail as its product name,
  - a fresh install uses `ProgramData\ArzoieMail`.
- `IniFileLocation` was updated for the two-folder lookup.
- The Administrator finds translations by their exact English text. A check confirmed that every English string mentioning the product still matches between `english.ini` and the C# source. The one existing mismatch, `String_43`, predates this PR.

## Not in this PR

- The documentation book (`hmailserver/documentation`) still says hMailServer throughout.
- WebAdmin (PHP) branding.
- Logos and icons.

commit.message:
Rebrand the product as ArzoieMail

Everything users see now says ArzoieMail, and fresh installations go to their own
folders. The identifiers that existing installations, scripts and WebAdmin depend on
keep their hMailServer names.

Renamed
- Installer: AppName, publisher, setup file name (ArzoieMail-<ver>-B<n>-x64),
  Programs and Features entry, Start menu group and shortcuts, messages. The
  "requires Windows" message now says Windows 10 instead of Vista SP2.
- New installations go to Program Files\ArzoieMail and ProgramData\ArzoieMail.
- Service display name ArzoieMail, also applied to an existing service on upgrade.
- Version resources and assembly metadata (product and company).
- Administrator, DBSetup, DBUpdater, DataDirectorySynchronizer and shared dialog
  text, and the same strings in all 38 translation files, kept in step because the
  Administrator looks translations up by their English text.
- CI artifact, release and tag names.

Kept as hMailServer
- The installer AppId, so that it upgrades an hMailServer installation in place.
- The service name and NT SERVICE\hMailServer, the hMailServer.Application COM API,
  hMailServer.exe and hMailServer.ini, registry keys, X-hMailServer-* headers, and the
  historical version names DBUpdater lists.

The server, the installer and the tests look for hMailServer.ini in
ProgramData\ArzoieMail first and then in ProgramData\hMailServer, which upgraded
installations keep. The installer recognises both the old and new tool window titles.

New regression tests (Infrastructure\ProductIdentity) check the service name, its
display name, the executable's product name and the new ProgramData folder.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
